Represents the biomass and nitrogen content of plant organs in APSIM Next Generation. This model provides a structured container to store, manipulate, and report biomass and nitrogen pools used throughout the Plant Modelling Framework (PMF). [\[csiroau-my...epoint.com\]](https://csiroau-my.sharepoint.com/personal/zhe00a_csiro_au/Documents/Working/04-Software/032-ApsimX/ApsimX/Models/PMF/Biomass/Biomass.cs?web=1)

## Overview

The Biomass model is a core data structure within APSIM NG, designed to hold the state of plant dry matter and nitrogen in a consistent and biologically meaningful way. It divides biomass into three pools:

* Structural biomass: long-lived tissue forming organ structure
* Storage biomass: non-structural reserves available for remobilisation
* Metabolic biomass: short-lived, actively metabolising tissue

Each of these pools has a corresponding nitrogen component, ensuring that both dry matter and nitrogen are tracked consistently.

The model itself does not simulate physiological processes such as growth or senescence. Instead, it serves as a container and mathematical utility to support other models that calculate biomass production, allocation, and redistribution. [\[csiroau-my...epoint.com\]](https://csiroau-my.sharepoint.com/personal/zhe00a_csiro_au/Documents/Working/04-Software/032-ApsimX/ApsimX/Models/PMF/Biomass/Biomass.cs?web=1)

Biologically, this structure reflects plant function where:

* Structural biomass contributes to physical integrity
* Storage biomass acts as a buffer during stress or surplus supply
* Metabolic biomass supports active growth processes

This separation enables APSIM to simulate complex plant behaviour while maintaining mass balance.

## Processes and Algorithms

{{< include /\_includes/Models/processes-intro.md >}}

### Biomass aggregation

Total biomass is calculated as:

$$
Wt = StructuralWt + StorageWt + MetabolicWt
$$

Total nitrogen is calculated as:

$$
N = StructuralN + StorageN + MetabolicN
$$

These relationships ensure mass balance across all biomass pools.

### Nitrogen concentration

Overall nitrogen concentration:

$$
NConc =
\begin{cases}
\frac{N}{Wt}, & \text{if } Wt > 0 \\
0, & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$

Pool-specific concentrations:

$$
StructuralNConc = \frac{StructuralN}{StructuralWt}
$$

$$
StorageNConc = \frac{StorageN}{StorageWt}
$$

$$
MetabolicNConc = \frac{MetabolicN}{MetabolicWt}
$$

These formulations prevent division by zero and ensure stable numerical behaviour. [\[csiroau-my...epoint.com\]](https://csiroau-my.sharepoint.com/personal/zhe00a_csiro_au/Documents/Working/04-Software/032-ApsimX/ApsimX/Models/PMF/Biomass/Biomass.cs?web=1)

### Biomass arithmetic operations

The class provides operations used throughout APSIM:

* Addition (combine biomass):

$$
B_{new} = B_1 + B_2
$$

* Subtraction (remove biomass):

$$
B_{new} = B_1 - B_2
$$

* Scaling (proportional allocation):

$$
B_{new} = f \cdot B
$$

* Reset:
  All pools are set to zero.

These operations are applied element-wise across structural, storage, and metabolic pools for both dry matter and nitrogen. [\[csiroau-my...epoint.com\]](https://csiroau-my.sharepoint.com/personal/zhe00a_csiro_au/Documents/Working/04-Software/032-ApsimX/ApsimX/Models/PMF/Biomass/Biomass.cs?web=1)

### Numerical stability

All values assigned to biomass pools are passed through a rounding function that sets very small values to zero. This avoids accumulation of floating-point errors and ensures physically meaningful results. [\[csiroau-my...epoint.com\]](https://csiroau-my.sharepoint.com/personal/zhe00a_csiro_au/Documents/Working/04-Software/032-ApsimX/ApsimX/Models/PMF/Biomass/Biomass.cs?web=1)

## User Interface

Biomass can be added as a child of a Plant or organ node in the model tree. Right-click the parent node, select "Add Model...", and search for Biomass in the Filter Box.

## Practical Example

The Biomass model is typically used within plant organs to track growth and nitrogen dynamics.

For example, in a leaf organ:

* Photosynthesis produces assimilates that increase storage biomass
* Structural growth transfers material from storage to structural pools
* Nitrogen uptake increases corresponding nitrogen pools
* Senescence removes biomass using subtraction operations

This allows APSIM to maintain consistent accounting of biomass and nitrogen during plant growth and development.
